about: Hand-labelled form fields on scanned (image-only, no AcroForm) pages, read by eye from the rendered page images with each source box drawn on them; seeded from the source PDFs' widgets, then every field was checked against the printed page. 'page' is the page of the scan (1-based). 'kind' is 'text' or 'checkbox' (a dropdown is a text field; a comb of single-character cells is one field per widget). 'box' is [x0, top, x1, bottom] in points, top-left origin, the area a person writes in or marks. 'caption' is the shortest printed text that unambiguously names the field (for a checkbox option, the option's text); a detected field's caption is right when the normalized caption, or any normalized 'accept' alternate, is contained in its accessible name (aria, else label text). 'widget' is the source PDF field name (or null for a visible blank that has no widget). A label with 'invisible': true is a widget with no visible cue on the printed page (no line, box, square or blank cell a person would write in): it is excluded from recall and precision. A label with 'optional': true is a visible blank that could fairly be detected or not (it has no widget, e.g. a signature line): a detection that matches it is neither a hit nor a false positive, and it does not count against recall. Matching rule: same page and kind, and the label's centre inside the detected box grown by 3 points, taken greedily one-to-one by highest IoU. Forms: fw9-scan is samples/scan.pdf (Form W-9, six pages, only page 1 has fields); i9-scan is samples/scan-i9.pdf (Form I-9 pages 1, 3, 4); w4-scan is samples/scan-w4.pdf (Form W-4 pages 1, 3, 4). Real scans: census1970-scan (pages 1 and 2 of samples/scan-census-1970.pdf) and census1960-scan (pages 2 and 4 of samples/scan-census-1960.pdf) are physical paper scans of US Census Bureau questionnaires, with the source URL in each entry. They have no widgets, so no source to seed from: every box was measured by eye on page images drawn with a 20-point grid in the page's own point units, repeated rows (the eight person rows of the 1970 roster, the 1960 fuel table) were placed with the measured row pitch, each label box was then drawn back over the page and checked, and the pages were swept for blanks without a box. The rules' output was not used to seed them. Write-in blanks (text, including dotted and dashed leaders), squares and fill-in circles (both 'checkbox') are labelled. The 1970 page 1 circles were NOT measured independently of the rules, unlike everything above: they were seeded from the rules' own circle detections, folded over the eight person rows (pitch 70.45 pt) into one template of 52 circles a row, then drawn back over the page and swept by eye for circles the rules missed and marks that are no circle; the boxes are the template's positions, not the detections' boxes. So a circle that is missed here is a real miss, but precision on circles is not an independent measure, and recall is an upper bound on how many the rules find that nothing found. The 24 circles of the 'DO NOT MARK THIS COLUMN' strip are 'optional' (office use). The 1970 page 2 circles are labelled after the rules were frozen (see scripts/eval_scan_fields.py HOLDOUT). The three name blanks on the 1970 page 2 sit under a printed heading in the same band, so they are 'optional'. 'real': true reports an entry in its own row of scripts/eval_scan_fields.py, apart from the synthetic forms.
